Topic: Carry-over: the rule catches unfair but cannot certify fair
Story (story.md): Opens by restating the Ch 2 surprise-zone rule and its blind spot: 52% bias is nearly invisible at N=100. The rule's strength depends on how much data you have.
Technical (chapter.md): Carried-from-Ch 2: rejection rule catches large biases, misses small ones. Now plan N to catch a specific bias.

Topic: Real institutions set N on purpose
Story (story.md): Drug trials (3000 vs 40 patients), polls (1000 calls, +/-3pp margin), A/B tests (millions of users for 0.25pp lift). Each pre-computes a target N.
Technical (chapter.md): Hunch (Loop B): huge tech companies run huge trials because their effects are tiny. 0.5pp lift on 5% baseline is real money.

Topic: Power = probability the rule fires when the bias is real
Story (story.md): Picks bias=0.55, tosses 100, asks how often the surprise rule catches it. Answer ~17%, misses ~5 times out of 6.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Try/Observe: for p=0.55 vs null p=0.5, N=100 gives power ~17%, N=1000 gives 88%, N=10000 essentially 1. Vocabulary: power = 1 - beta.

Topic: Power curve at linear axis crushes the interesting region
Story (story.md): Sweeps N from 10 to 5000 at bias=0.55. Climb bunches against the left edge. Image story/detection_grows_linear.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered (pedagogical linear-first framing is story-only).

Topic: Log-scale x-axis lets the small-N climb breathe
Story (story.md): Same data, log x-axis. S-shaped curve, annotated: 100 tosses -> 17%, 780 tosses -> 80%, 2000 tosses -> essentially 100%. Image story/detection_grows_log.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Observe: power curves plotted on log-N axis with an 80% reference line. Image power_curves.png.

Topic: 80% power is a convention, not a law
Story (story.md): Willing to miss 1 in 5 if you catch the other 4. 95% used when missing is unacceptable, 50% when you just want better than chance.
Technical (chapter.md): Vocabulary (Loop A): 80% conventional, 95% if you cannot afford to miss. Asymmetry note: stricter alpha lowers power at fixed N.

Topic: Bigger effects need less data
Story (story.md): Five curves overlaid: 0.7 climbs almost immediately, 0.51 barely reaches 80% even at N=100000. Image story/detection_at_different_biases.png. Grandmother-glasses analogy.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Probe: tiny bias p=0.51 only reaches power ~0.52 at N=10000; obvious bias p=0.70 at N=50 already decent.

Topic: Required N, the inverse question
Story (story.md): For each candidate bias, find the smallest N hitting 80% detection. Linear-y hockey stick. Image story/required_n_linear.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Try/Observe: invert Loop A. For each truth p, find smallest N at 80% and 95% power. Image required_n.png.

Topic: Log-y axis reveals the power-law structure
Story (story.md): Same curve on log-y. Landmarks: bias 0.7 -> 50 tosses; 0.6 -> 200; 0.55 -> 780; 0.52 -> 5000; 0.51 -> 20000. Image story/required_n_log.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Observe: p=0.51 needs ~19600 tosses, p=0.52 needs ~4900, p=0.55 needs ~783, p=0.60 needs ~200, p=0.70 needs ~50.

Topic: Required N scales like 1/effect^2
Story (story.md): Halving the bias quadruples the required N. Tech companies need millions because their effects are tiny.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Formula sketch: n approx (z_{alpha/2}+z_beta)^2 sigma^2 / delta^2. At alpha=0.05, beta=0.2 the prefactor is ~7.85; for p0=0.5, delta=0.05 gives ~785 matching simulation.
Code: SKIP: formula sketch, no separate code

Topic: Tech-company A/B math
Story (story.md): 5% baseline, 0.25pp lift needs ~24000 users; 0.125pp lift needs ~100000; 0.1pp lift needs several hundred thousand.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Hunch: why tech companies care about N.

Topic: Small studies claiming small effects are suspect
Story (story.md): A 40-patient 3-month study claiming a 5% improvement is, by this math, essentially incapable of detecting an effect that small. Either the effect was bigger or the result is a fluke.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered (policy framing is story-only).

Topic: Replication is not pooling
Story (story.md): Run the 780-toss experiment 10 times at bias=0.55 across 1000 groups. Bars peak at 7/8/9 catches, but ~30 groups catch only 5, some catch all 10. Image story/replication_distribution.png. Pooling all 7800 tosses would hit ~100% detection.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered (replication framing is story-only).

Topic: Replication crisis and independence
Story (story.md): Replication means independent attempts, not more data. Five independent labs each running a 40-patient study is stronger than one 200-patient study. Tobacco-funded labs are not independent witnesses.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered.

Topic: MDE: smallest catchable effect at fixed N
Story (story.md): Three-panel progression: linear, x-log, both-log. Log-log is a straight line with slope: quadruple N, halve MDE. Image story/mde_progression.png. Landmarks: N=100 -> 11pp; N=1000 -> 3.5pp; N=10000 -> 1pp; N=100000 -> 0.33pp.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Try/Observe: N=100 detects ~12pp, N=1000 ~4pp, N=10000 ~1.3pp, N=100000 ~0.4pp (one-sided; two-sided slightly larger). Image mde_curve.png. Hunch: MDE and required-N are the same machinery, inverted.

Topic: Three knobs linked: threshold, bias, target, N
Story (story.md): Three-panel triptych, each fixes two knobs and varies a third. Loose alpha=10% crosses 80% at ~500 tosses, default 5% at ~780, strict 1% at ~1400. Image story/three_knobs.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Vocabulary note: asymmetry between alpha and power. Covered implicitly across Loops A-C.

Topic: No free lunch
Story (story.md): Cannot have tight threshold, small bias, small N, and high power all at once. Pick three, the fourth is determined. Drug trials, polls, A/B tests live on this tradeoff.
Technical (chapter.md): Implicit across Loop B formula.

Topic: Bayesian stopping rule: stop when the posterior is narrow enough
Story (story.md): Keep tossing until the 95% belief band is no wider than 4 points. For truth=0.55, this lands around 2400 tosses.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Try/Observe: 200 runs, target 95% CI width <= 0.04, truth=0.55. Median stop 2380 with stops in [2340, 2400]. Granularity is from checking every 20 tosses. Image bayes_stopping.png.

Topic: Precision target vs hypothesis-test target
Story (story.md): 780 tosses answers 'catch 0.55 bias 80% of the time'; 2400 answers 'pin bias down to +/-2pp'. Different questions, not in the same ballpark.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Compare: fixed N for 95% CI of width 0.04 is n approx 4 z^2 p(1-p)/w^2 ~ 2377, matching the Bayesian median (2380). 783-toss 80% power is a different question (half-width ~0.035).

Topic: Peeking breaks frequentist alpha, not Bayesian posteriors
Story (story.md): Non-peeking frequentist rule sets the 5% false-alarm budget; peek-and-stop on fair coins inflates that rate well above 5%.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Edge case: 2000 fair-coin runs of N=1000 tosses peeking every 10, stopping on first p<0.05 rejects ~33% of the time. Likelihood principle: posterior summaries are invariant to stopping rule; Bayes factors against a point null are not. Image peeking_rejection.png.

Topic: Freq vs Bayes reach the same decision most of the time
Story (story.md): 4 bias panels (0.50/0.52/0.55/0.60) x 3 sample sizes (50/200/1000) x 1000 experiments. Agreement above 90% everywhere; highest disagreement in borderline regions. Image story/freq_vs_bayes_decisions.png. Companies often switch back to frequentist because the ship/no-ship decisions matched 8 times in 10.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Method note: Loops A-C use normal_approx_power, Loop D stopping uses exact Beta posterior. Different machinery answering different questions.

Topic: 'No evidence of harm' is not 'no harm'
Story (story.md): Fluoride case study: a null result could mean a well-powered study found nothing, or a small study missed a small effect, or the wrong effect was measured. Same headline, three very different statements. MDE is the right question to ask of any policy study.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered (policy framing is story-only).

Topic: Hand-off: same data, different tests, different verdicts?
Story (story.md): Closing flag: exact binomial, normal-approx z, chi-square, Fisher exact, t-test on the fraction, Bayesian variants. When do they agree?
Technical (chapter.md): Big question: same data, multiple tests -- when do they reach different conclusions? Opens Ch 4.
